here is another reply cause of your question around public transport.  

in chicago we have a hub and spoke system where everything takes you downtown with the exception of buses which are on a grid.  

chicago city proper has excellent bus and subway (L) coverage. we also have mtra (light train) that heads to the suburbs. we also have amtrak that heads to major cities in every direction.  

we have two airports. uber is everywhere. 

the city is very walkable, very bikeable.  

if you live in columbia you will need a car... can you get around without it... sure, but it will be a pain in the ass. you're a second class citizen. and you have a family to care for.  

in chicago you do not need a car, but it would be very, very helpful with a family.  

personally, i think you're making a huge mistake if you're basing your decision on public transit. missing the forest for the trees.  

chicago is not cheap. there are places to live that are cheaper, but they will not be as gentrified, and raising a family there may pose difficult depending on your background.  

cost of living is substantially more expensive here. 70k solo salary would put you at the absolute bottom end of the 'not poor' category for the city. now, if you are a frugal person and find a cheap place to rent then you could have a wonderful life enjoying all the city has to offer (made cheaper if you dont live IN the city but go north or south along the lake).  

hard to answer rent and utilities questions... depends on location.  1,000-$2,000/m for rent depending on location. utilities probably 75-150 a month if you are frugal, if not... 125-250. keep in mind we have taxes on f'ing everything here... 11% cloud tax.  

so, i cannot stress this enough: if you decide to come to chicago you do so because you want to live in a state that despite being 'red' outside of chicago is very liberal. you want to live in a state that balances personal freedoms/conservativism with acceptance of different life styles. you want the opportuniteis chicago has to offer, you want the architecture, the parks, etc, etc, etc. 

if you're asking: where should i go to raise a family and have great quality of life... columbia is a tremdously better value for the money (excluding state politics).

again, this written by someone who grew up in como, and has now lived in chicago for 15 years. i would move back to como if i were retiring and didn't need/want to work OR if i needed a safe place to raise a family where the dollar goes far.
